What the auditor will ask: What is inside and outside the ISMS, and why?
Evidence to show: isms-scope.md

What the auditor will ask: Is there an approved policy, and do staff know about it?
Evidence to show: information-security-policy.md signed by the CEO; staff acknowledgement at onboarding
Notes: Policy approved. Staff acknowledgement list still missing.

What the auditor will ask: Who is the ISMS Manager, and who owns each risk?
Evidence to show: Role description signed by the CEO; risk owners named in the register
Notes: Owners are named in the register. Signed role description missing.

What the auditor will ask: How do you identify and rate risks?
Evidence to show: risk-assessment-method.md (5x5 scale, thresholds, due dates)

What the auditor will ask: Show the results and when they were last reviewed.
Evidence to show: risk-register.xlsx (30 risks); yearly review record
Notes: Add a dated review note at each yearly review.

What the auditor will ask: What will you do about each risk, who owns it, and by when?
Evidence to show: Treatment, planned control, owner and due date columns in the risk register

What the auditor will ask: Which controls apply, and why are others excluded?
Evidence to show: statement-of-applicability.xlsx (93 controls with reasons)

What the auditor will ask: What are your objectives, and how do you track them?
Evidence to show: Objectives in the policy; quarterly progress note per objective
Notes: Objectives exist. Progress tracking starts with the first quarterly report.

What the auditor will ask: Is the ISMS Manager trained for the role?
Evidence to show: Training or certificate records for the ISMS Manager
Notes: Needs training or an ISO 27001 course for the part-time IT administrator.

What the auditor will ask: How are documents versioned, approved and kept current?
Evidence to show: Version numbers, approval lines and Git history; list of ISMS documents
Notes: Git history exists. Add a document list to the README.

What the auditor will ask: How do you know the ISMS works?
Evidence to show: Quarterly report: open risks by level, MFA coverage, training completion, patch compliance, incidents

What the auditor will ask: Show the audit programme and the last internal audit report.
Evidence to show: Audit plan, report with findings, follow-up actions
Notes: Independent person needed. Consider an external consultant.

What the auditor will ask: Show the minutes of the last management review.
Evidence to show: Minutes with inputs (risks, incidents, audit results) and decisions

What the auditor will ask: How do you record and fix problems?
Evidence to show: Log of findings, causes, actions, owners and closure dates

What the auditor will ask: Show the last quarterly access review for Azure, GitHub and the database.
Evidence to show: Signed review sheet: accounts, roles, changes made, reviewer, date

What the auditor will ask: Show the checklists for the last three leavers.
Evidence to show: Completed leaver checklists with dates; Entra ID audit log showing the account disabled
Notes: Checklist must also cover GitHub, Azure and the support tool (R13).

What the auditor will ask: How many accounts use MFA, and can any account skip it?
Evidence to show: Entra ID authentication methods report; Conditional Access policy screenshot
Notes: MFA is on email for some staff only today.

What the auditor will ask: Who are the administrators, and how do they sign in?
Evidence to show: Admin role list; passkey or security key registration; break-glass account test record
Notes: Also covers R10, the single point of failure.

What the auditor will ask: How are passwords managed?
Evidence to show: Password manager rollout record; Entra ID password policy settings

What the auditor will ask: Who can reach customer data, and from where?
Evidence to show: Azure SQL network settings (private endpoints), role assignments, quarterly configuration review

What the auditor will ask: How do you stop secrets and unreviewed code reaching production?
Evidence to show: GitHub settings: branch protection, required review, secret scanning, push protection, SSO and MFA

What the auditor will ask: Show who was trained and how phishing tests went.
Evidence to show: Attendance list; phishing simulation results; onboarding checklist
Notes: Training is the main fix for the top risk, phishing.

What the auditor will ask: How do staff report incidents, and show the incident log.
Evidence to show: Reporting channel and mailbox; incident log (or a statement that none occurred)

What the auditor will ask: Have you practised the response?
Evidence to show: Tabletop exercise report with actions and owners
Notes: First exercise by 17 January 2027 (see the incident response policy).

What the auditor will ask: What is logged, for how long, and who looks at alerts?
Evidence to show: Defender for Cloud settings; log retention configuration; a sample alert and response
Notes: Only basic Azure activity logs today.

What the auditor will ask: Have you tested that you can restore?
Evidence to show: Restore test report with time taken against the recovery targets

What the auditor will ask: How quickly are critical updates installed, and is protection active?
Evidence to show: Patch compliance report (14-day target); Defender coverage report

What the auditor will ask: Are laptops encrypted and phones protected?
Evidence to show: Device compliance report: disk encryption, screen lock; app protection policy for work email on phones
Notes: Also covers R05, lost or stolen laptops.

What the auditor will ask: Show the supplier register and the checks on key suppliers.
Evidence to show: Supplier register; security reviews for the payment, support and backup suppliers; data processing agreements

What the auditor will ask: Show your record of processing and how requests are handled.
Evidence to show: Record of processing activities; data subject request log with 30-day tracking; data processing agreements

What the auditor will ask: Does NIS2 apply to you, and how did you decide?
Evidence to show: Written applicability assessment with the conclusion and date

What the auditor will ask: Show the list of your information assets.
Evidence to show: Inventory of systems, data and devices with owners
Notes: Assets are in the risk register only today.

What the auditor will ask: What rules do staff follow, and did they accept them?
Evidence to show: Published rules; staff acknowledgement list

What the auditor will ask: Do contracts state security duties?
Evidence to show: Contract template with confidentiality and security clauses
Notes: Contracts exist. Security duties are not yet explicit.

What the auditor will ask: Who can enter the office, and how are visitors recorded?
Evidence to show: Visitor sign-in sheet; key list; quarterly review
